critical_code_review_comments: MakerDetail.jsx lines 112-113: Both redirect and sectionMissing use <Navigate replace> — clean solution, no history pollution when hitting an old slug or unknown slug. Uses sectionsData.redirects map to migrate old slugs → new slugs before falling back to root.

MakerDetail.jsx line 60-63: `shownProducts` filter runs client-side against the already-fetched products list — this is what makes navigation feel instant and preserves SPA state (verified via window.__spa_marker__ surviving nav). Nice.
StoreSectionsTab.jsx uses HTML5 native drag/drop for reorder — works but does not have visual drop indicator; consider adding a subtle drop-zone highlight for accessibility. Non-blocking.
SectionEditor initializes `selected` from products.filter — correctly reads p.section_slugs which is the canonical membership source-of-truth on the product doc. Good.

useStructuredData in MakerDetail is called BEFORE the early-return `if (redirectTo)` — since react hooks order matters, this is safe because the same hook is called on every render, but the JSON-LD is set for the pre-redirect state momentarily. In practice the redirect fires immediately so no user impact. Consider guarding the jsonLd payload with a conditional to skip when redirectTo is truthy.
StoreSectionsTab confirm() uses window.confirm — native browser dialog. Fine for maker dashboard but inconsistent with the app's toast/UI language. Non-blocking; low priority.
MakerDetail lines 419-436 and 439-462: the mobile tabs and desktop sidebar both call the same `sections`+`sectionsData.all_count` — DRY-friendly, single source of truth per render.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (9/9 flows: manager CRUD, editor picker persistence, desktop sidebar SPA nav + counts + breadcrumbs + canonical, mobile tabs SPA nav, deep link, unknown-slug redirect, backwards-compat, listings-tab regression, product-card click)
